current_answer: As of 7 October 2026, public evidence does not establish a broad capability decline across popular AI models or a confirmed Claude Opus 5.5 decline. OpenAI reported two separate product issues: a ChatGPT Work desktop-app version prevented creation of new Work threads, and Workspace Agents had degraded responses. Both were marked resolved; OpenAI said affected Work users should update the app. These are availability and product-path findings, not model-quality measurements. The 6 October GPT-5.6 Sol High complaint remains one unverified user report without a task replay or served-model receipt, and no link to either incident has been shown. BridgeBench's latest displayed Opus 5.5 result remains 96.5% of launch power on 4 October, within its own 90–110% band; it combines task performance, tokens, and cost. LiveNerf has 13/30 daily collections and no post-baseline comparison, while a closed issue reports a window-boundary problem that may prevent its preregistered decision rule from firing. Suggested next step: update the affected Work app if relevant; for a completed answer that seems weaker, preserve the task, settings, surface, and displayed model, then replay it against a dated baseline after service recovery.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad model decline is established. Two specific OpenAI product issues were resolved; neither is a quality test.

summary: No broad capability decline across popular models is established by the reviewed public evidence.
OpenAI marked a version-specific ChatGPT Work desktop issue resolved after releasing an app fix; affected users should update. The issue blocked creation of new Work threads.
A separate Workspace Agents issue affected whether users saw agent responses and was marked recovered. Neither incident measures model quality or connects to the 6 October Reddit complaint.
The GPT-5.6 Sol High complaint remains a single unverified report without a task receipt, exact client, route, verified served model, or replay.
BridgeBench's latest Opus 5.5 result is 96.5% of launch power on 4 October, within its stated 90–110% band; the measure combines task score, tokens, and cost.

LiveNerf shows 13/30 days and no comparison result. A closed issue reports a window-boundary flaw that may block its preregistered two-window decision rule; no linked fix or resolution note was visible.
Suggested: update the affected Work app; for a weaker completed answer, save the task, settings, surface, and displayed model, then replay against a dated baseline after recovery.
uncertainty: The 6 October ChatGPT complaint is self-reported and includes no prompt, task result, exact client, route, or independently verified served model.
The two OpenAI product incidents concern Work thread creation and Workspace Agent responses; no evidence links them to the separate ChatGPT conversation complaint.
Provider status pages report aggregate service state, not individual account impact or answer quality.
BridgeBench's 96.5% is a vendor-defined composite within its stated variance band and is not a capability-only estimate.
LiveNerf's latest status has no post-baseline result. Issue #9 is closed, but the repository page showed no linked pull request or resolution note for the reported window-boundary bug.
The search found no new independently checkable task receipt in Spanish or Chinese; a small discovery search cannot measure audience prevalence.
Analytics are unavailable, so reader visits, return use, sharing, and funding outcomes are unobserved.
freshness_note: Checked 7 October 2026. Two provider-reported product issues are marked resolved. They do not establish model capability change; the latest user quality report has no matched replay. A public tracker also has an unverified windowing correction concern.
